250 years ago, a group of startup founders had a bold idea. They were obsessed with the user. Every decision came back to what citizens actually needed. They had a unique insight nobody else was betting on: people could govern themselves. Free markets could work. They did things that don’t scale. Washington was a general (a technical founder) on the front lines with his troops. Their first version flopped. The Articles of Confederation couldn’t hold the company together. So they hard-pivoted and wrote the Constitution. Then they never stopped shipping. 27 amendments and counting. The lesson remains: talk to your users, stay close to the work, and don’t be afraid to throw out v1. Happy 4th!!!!🇺🇸

QA is dead. Or at least, the old way of doing it is. AI now writes all your code. Does it still work? That's the gap: coding agents are scaling output exponentially, and bugs and incidents are scaling right alongside it. The best QA are the ones who know everything about your product: every edge case, every piece of business logic. Today, we give that knowledge to Momentic's most capable agent. Every Jira and Linear ticket, one-off threads in Slack, designs in Figma, PRDs in Notion, every PR and commit - Momentic knows all. In just the past few weeks, our agents analyzed over 70,000 test failures and created 600 tests, with a 73% merge rate that's climbing fast. We're grateful for the trust of our customers: some of the world's best engineering teams, including Notion , Xero , Webflow , Retool , Runway , Bilt rely on Momentic’s critical infrastructure every day.

This is how Stellar Sleep pulled us out of pivot hell. We'd been stuck for weeks. Trying idea after idea. Nothing stuck because we had no conviction in any of it. We are close friends with the Stellar Sleep team. They work on the same floor as us. So during pivot hell, I'd talk to them every day, just chatting about whatever we were poking at. One day we showed them a super sloppy internal tool we'd built for our last company. Unexpectedly, they said they’d pay for it over HelpScout. The next week, we packaged it into an AI native support platform called Letterbook (YC S23) . And when their team made it their daily driver, that gave us the conviction we needed. We spent weeks searching for a way out of pivot hell. Turns out it was just sitting a few desks over.

Ethan Hou and I are off to NYC for 2 weeks! We want to meet consumer founders scaling fast. We’d love to trade notes on B2C growth from our last startup Martin (YC S23) , on topics like Meta Ads, UGC, and App Store growth. And, we want to learn about your customer support and operations problems as you’re growing! If you’re up for a productive cup of coffee, DMs are open.

Does customer support matter at a B2C company with PMF? When you have 100 users, obviously yes. You treat each user as a B2B contract, and hopefully, they become super-referrers like the first 100 Airbnb users. But what if you have 10,000 users? Is it no longer worth your time? Maybe before, when you had to spend months training human agents, but with AI, it's easier than ever to scale founder-grade customer support infinitely. AI support agents like Letterbook (YC S23) can: - Solve complicated data or payment issues like a founder - Write concise and accurate responses like a founder - Respond within minutes like a founder And when every user gets founder-grade support, good things happen! 1. Your virality coefficient increases. More 5-star ratings and fewer scathing reviews mean people convert! (The most common bad review is this company's customer support sucks). 2. Your churn decreases. You will retain a considerable proportion of unhappy customers by solving their issues and responding instantly. 3. You stand out from the competition. The biggest company in your industry is guaranteed to have bad customer support. So yes, it matters! Take 15 minutes to set up an AI support agent, and beat companies like the one in the screenshot!

I met ~50 college dropouts at an event last month. It felt like meeting 50 copies of myself from 3 years ago, except much better equipped for the road ahead of them. When I left college to do YC, there were hardly any teams my age. That year, I turned 20, raised a seed round, had 2 co-founders leave, and struggled for months to find just 100 active users for our app. To the newly dropped-out founders, I think you’ll kill it. Just 2 small bits of advice: 1. If you find yourself uttering the words “we’re cooked”, that is normal. We are all in fact cooked. My DMs are always open if you want to chat. 2. If you happen to be next Zuck and hit 1m ARR in 3 months, I’m sure you’re getting bombarded with customer support tickets. In that case, you really should hit up our AI support agent: https://letterbook.ai
